value: class mapping table: the consequence-class vocabulary of capabilities.json, mapped to C0-C5

SPECIFICATION. This file IS the class mapping table that 05 section 11 and 08 section 1 name as one of the six protected control objects. Changing it is a C5 protected control change, carried by ConfigurationVersion with control_object_kind = class_mapping_table.

F6A-06. `ConsequenceDerivation.declared_floor_ref` is REQUIRED and the class set is computed "from the owning capability contract's declared floor, and from nothing else" -- and capabilities.json had no floor field of any name, zero occurrences of any C0-C5 token, and a 53-term free-text vocabulary with nothing anywhere mapping it onto the six classes. An implementer populating that required field for CAP-17, CAP-22 or CAP-24 had no rule for which class definition to point at, and two implementers would map 53 terms onto six classes differently -- a mapping that decides WHO MAY ACT. The table was named three times across two chapters and did not exist.

A capability's `declared_floor` is the HIGHEST class its declared terms map to. Read that narrowly: it is a floor, a single class that always applies to any action under the capability, and it is NOT the total rank the design refuses. 02 section 4 forbids collapsing a REACHED SET into one class and applying one row -- that is AT-M4-02 and it drops C2's human requirement on an action that is both C2 and C3. This computation runs over a capability's declared vocabulary at design time and produces ONE OF THE FOUR INPUTS to the derivation, whose output is still a set and whose every member's gates still apply. The two are different objects and only the second is the one the prohibition is about.
validate_contracts.py: every term any capability declares is mapped here, and every mapped term is declared by some capability
validate_contracts.py: every capability's declared_floor equals the maximum of its mapped terms
validate_contracts.py: CAP-13, CAP-14, CAP-15 and CAP-16 floor at C3, which is what 05 section 11 states in prose
validate_contracts.py: ConsequenceDerivation.declared_floor_ref targets ConsequenceClassDefinition, whose class_id is drawn from the same six
S1-C01, through a ProtectedChange whose protected_subject_kind is class_mapping_table

acceptance.reason: Recording that work was accepted is an internal state change on records the company already holds; it creates no destination, promise or production write.

allocation.reason: Assigning internal capacity, budget headroom or a lane is a controlled internal mutation; the money it may later authorise is `financial`, mapped separately.

attention.reason: Founder attention is allocated internally. The scarcity is real and the act is an internal assignment.

authority.reason: Who may act is the protected-control-change class by name: identity roots and the grant and interpretation machinery.

availability.reason: Keeping or restoring a service available is a production effect with reversibility and containment conditions.

closure.reason: Closing a venture settles duties, entitlements and money with outside parties; every closure step is economic or contractual before it is anything else.

code.reason: Code is a production and environment effect the moment it is anything but a draft, and C4's row names deployment first.

collaboration.reason: Collaboration reaches a party outside the acting component, so a destination and a purpose exist.

competence.reason: A competence determination is recorded internally; the professional prerequisites it gates are `professional`, mapped separately.

compute.reason: Metered compute is spend against a real account. An allowance that runs out is money, not a counter.

contact.reason: External contact IS the C2 row: exact destination, data, purpose and relationship constraints.

containment.reason: Containing an incident is a production and security action with descendants and reversibility conditions.

continuity.reason: Continuity arrangements are production and access arrangements that must survive the person who made them.

contract.reason: A contract is the economic/contractual class stated in one word.

credential.reason: A credential is delegated access, which C4's row names explicitly; the machinery that issues one is `authority`, mapped at C5.

customer-promise.reason: A promise to a customer is a binding commitment, which is the C3 row.

customer-service.reason: Answering a customer is an outward message to a named recipient.

customer-terms.reason: Terms are the contract, expressed as the thing the customer agreed to.

decision-support.reason: Assembling material for a decision is deterministic work over already authorized data; the decision itself is classified by what it decides.

deletion.reason: Deletion is a destructive state change, which C4's row names, and it is not undone by a revert.

deployment.reason: Deployment is the first example in C4's own row.

direction.reason: Endorsed direction is an internal record whose effect on outside parties runs through the work it admits, never through itself.

disclosure.reason: Disclosure is the external-disclosure class by name.

employment.reason: Employing someone creates continuing economic and contractual duties to a person.

evidence.reason: Capturing evidence writes internal records; what the evidence is ABOUT is classified separately.

experiment.reason: An experiment that reaches real people is outreach; one that does not is `internal-analysis`, which the same capability also declares.

external-query.reason: A query to an outside source is an outward request with a destination.

financial-record.reason: Bookkeeping writes internal records; the payments they record are `financial` and the statutory filings are `reporting`.

governance.reason: Governance decides who decides, which is a protected control change.

grievance.reason: A grievance involves a person outside the company who must be reachable and must be answered.

identity.reason: Identity roots are named in C5's row.

improvement.reason: Proposing an improvement writes an internal record; ACTIVATING one is `self-change`, mapped at C5, and the two are deliberately different terms.

internal-analysis.reason: Deterministic work over already authorized data in an isolated workspace, which is C0's row verbatim.

internal-artifact.reason: A draft that has not left the workspace is local computation; putting it outside is `publication` or `disclosure`.

internal-record.reason: Writing an internal record is a controlled internal mutation.

knowledge.reason: Knowledge entries are internal records with an epoch and a writer.

legal.reason: A legal step creates or discharges a duty owed to someone, which is contractual before it is anything else.

opportunity-cost.reason: An opportunity cost is a judgement recorded against an internal allocation.

personal-data.reason: Personal data carries a category, a purpose, a destination and a retention rule, which is the C2 row's second half.

physical.reason: Physical performance is named in C4's row.

procurement.reason: Buying something commits money and creates a supplier relationship.

professional.reason: A professional determination is a competent determination with real-world prerequisites, which C4's row names; the fee for it is `financial`.

public-claims.reason: A public claim is a representation that binds the company to it. 05 section 11 floors CAP-13 at the economic/contractual class and `public-claims` is the only term of its three that can carry that floor.

publication.reason: Publishing puts data at an external destination.

readiness.reason: A readiness assessment is an internal record about whether something may proceed.

recovery.reason: Recovery machinery is named in C5's row alongside grant, release, capture and interpretation.

relationship.reason: A relationship is maintained through contact with a party outside the company.

remedy.reason: A remedy is a refund, a credit or a replacement, which is money or a new promise.

reporting.reason: A report goes to a recipient outside the acting component, including a statutory one.

security.reason: Security actions delegate or revoke access and change production state.

self-change.reason: The system changing itself is the protected-change class, and the reason 08 section 1 enumerates its six control objects.

succession.reason: Succession moves identity and authority roots to another party.
